links.outcome: Medical adequacy and completeness of ChatGPT-4o answers on established (PAP) versus recent (HGNS) therapy
links.effect: Medical adequacy was higher for PAP (mean 4.9) than HGNS (mean 4.6, p<0.05). Completeness was confirmed in 45/51 ratings (88.24%) for PAP and 28/51 (54.9%) for HGNS.
links.quote: However, some substantial flaws regarding second line HGNS therapy are most likely due to recent advances in HGNS therapy and the consequent limited information available in LLM training data.

screen.reason: The study evaluates ChatGPT-4o's capability to answer frequently asked questions by sleep apnea patients regarding PAP and HGNS therapies, assessed by clinical experts for adequacy, completeness, and potential hazard.
